---
title: "Drawing the dial"
description: "bauhaus_clock() draws the screensaver's dial itself with ggplot2."
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE,
  dev = "ragg_png",
  out.width = "100%"
)
library(ggplot2)
library(bauhaus)
```

`bauhaus_clock()` draws the dial of the screensaver as a ggplot, in any of the sixteen colourways:
the minute track and its numerals, the steel hour indices with their lume inlays, the hour numerals,
the three hands and their soft, tinted shadows, all on the grained plate.

The geometry follows the screensaver's measured design, with every length a fraction of the
distance from the centre to the end of the 12 o'clock index. Like the screensaver, it draws every
"1" as a plain capsule rather than the font's flagged glyph. The steel is drawn flat, without the
screensaver's per-pixel shading.

```{r turquoise, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 6, out.width = "75%", fig.align = "center"}
bauhaus_clock("turquoise")
```

## Saving

Everything on the dial, numerals included, is drawn as shapes, so it scales to any size. Save it
square:

```{r save, eval = FALSE}
ggsave("noir.png", bauhaus_clock("noir"), width = 4, height = 4, dpi = 300)
```

## Time

The default time, 10:08:13, is the one shown in the screensaver's reference renders. Pass a time as
`"HH:MM"`, `"HH:MM:SS"` or a date-time, for example `Sys.time()`:

```{r time, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
library(patchwork)

bauhaus_clock("salmon", time = "16:42:30") |
  bauhaus_clock("glacier", time = "07:15", seconds = FALSE)
```

## A simpler dial

Leave out the seconds hand and the minute numerals for a quieter face, or the grain for a flat
plate:

```{r simple, fig.width = 4, fig.height = 4, out.width = "50%", fig.align = "center"}
bauhaus_clock("lavender", time = "12:52", seconds = FALSE, minute_numerals = FALSE)
```

## All sixteen

```{r all, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 8}
clocks <- lapply(bauhaus_dial_names(), bauhaus_clock, minute_numerals = FALSE)
wrap_plots(clocks, ncol = 4) &
  theme(plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2))
```

## Building on the dial

The result is an ordinary ggplot, so you can add to it. The plot runs from -1.16 to 1.16 on both
axes (from -1.04 without the minute numerals), with the end of the 12 o'clock index at y = 1.

```{r annotate, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 6, out.width = "75%", fig.align = "center"}
col <- bauhaus_colours("pistachio")
bauhaus_clock("pistachio", time = "09:00", seconds = FALSE) +
  annotate("text",
    x = 0, y = -0.33, label = "ggplot2", colour = col[["track"]],
    family = bauhaus_font_family("semibold")
  )
```
